tag.name: Imports
tag.description: CSV imports. An import goes upload → setup (match columns, say where the contacts came from, choose topics) → safety check → import, and can be cancelled while it waits. Checking and importing run in the background: poll `GET /imports/{id}` until the status moves on. Every step needs brand admin; starting the import also needs step-up.

get.description: The brand's 20 most recent imports, newest first. Brand admins only.

post.description:
Starts an import from a CSV file (`multipart/form-data`, field `file`): at most 20 MB and 200,000 rows, UTF-8 (a BOM is fine), comma, semicolon or tab separated, with a header row and unique column names. Blank rows are skipped. The file is stored with the import, with the first 5 rows as a preview and a suggested column mapping (from common Mailchimp, Klaviyo and Shopify header names); nothing is imported yet. Brand admins only.

This is the one write that isn't JSON: browsers must send their `Origin` (one of the app's), as they always do with uploads.

An upload of more than 5,000 rows and over 3× the brand's current contacts raises an `import_spike` alert for the company.

file.description: The CSV export; its name (without any path) is kept as the import's `filename`.

400.description: `bad_file`: no file attached, the upload didn't finish or was too large, or the file can't be read as a CSV of contacts (not UTF-8, empty, no rows, a duplicated column, too many rows…). The message says which.

get.description: One import with its preview rows and the attestation text and consent sources the setup screen shows. Poll this while it's `checking` or `importing`. Brand admins only.

put.description:
Saves the column mapping, the answers about where the contacts came from, and the topics they'll be subscribed to. Only while the import is `uploaded`, `checked` or `failed`; saving puts it back to `uploaded` and clears any earlier check, so the check must run again. The consent answers aren't validated here: anything missing shows up as a problem in the safety check, which then fails.

Ticking `consent.attested` records the caller as the person who signed the attestation, and when; it's also written to the audit log (`import.attested`, with the attestation text, source and row count) as part of the consent proof. Brand admins only.

400.description: `bad_json`: the body isn't valid JSON for this call, or has unknown fields. `bad_mapping`: no email column, a column the file doesn't have, or `consent.tracking` is `column` without a `mapping.tracking` column. `no_topics`: choose at least one topic. `unknown_topic`: a topic doesn't belong to this brand.

409.description: `import_locked`: the import is being checked, imported, or is finished or cancelled, so it can't be changed.

post.description: Queues the safety check: every address is classified (invalid, duplicate, suppressed company-wide, role address, throwaway inbox, domain without a mail server, existing or unsubscribed contact, stale → quarantine, ready), and the import passes the gate only if the consent answers are complete, the invalid and role/throwaway shares are under the company's safety limits, and someone can be imported. The import becomes `checking`, then `checked` (see `check_result`) or `failed` (see `error`). Allowed from `uploaded`, `checked` or `failed`; no body. Brand admins only.

202.description: Queued; the import as it is now (`checking`, unless the check already finished).

400.description: `bad_mapping`: match the email column first (set the import up).

409.description: `import_busy`: it's already being checked or imported, or it's finished or cancelled.

post.description: Queues the import itself, if the last safety check passed. It runs in one transaction (all rows or none), re-reading suppressions and contacts since the check: new people are added as `subscribed` (or `quarantined` if stale) to the chosen topics, each with an `import_attested` consent record; existing contacts only get blanks filled in, tags and activity added (their status and consent never change); unsubscribed and suppressed people are left alone. The import becomes `importing`, then `done` (see `import_result`; the uploaded file is deleted) or `failed` with nothing imported. No body. Brand admins only, with step-up. Recorded in the audit log (`import.started`, then `import.finished`).

202.description: Queued; the import as it is now (`importing`, unless it already finished).

409.description: `not_checked`: run the safety check first (the import isn't `checked`). `import_gate_failed`: it didn't pass the safety check. `import_busy`: it's already running.

post.description: Cancels an import that's waiting (`uploaded`, `checked` or `failed`) and deletes the uploaded file. A check or import that's still running can only be cancelled once it's been stuck for 35 minutes (jobs time out at 30). No body. Brand admins only.

409.description: `import_busy`: it's finished or already cancelled, or still running and not stuck yet.

ImportsStatus.description: `uploaded`: waiting for setup or a check. `checking` / `importing`: running in the background. `checked`: see `check_result`. `failed`: see `error`; can be set up and checked again. `done` and `cancelled` are final.

preview.description: The file's first rows, as text, in the order of `import.headers`.

attestation_text.description: What the importer signs by ticking `consent.attested`.
examples: I confirm this list was not bought, rented, appended, scraped or shared by anyone else, and everyone on it agreed to hear from this brand.

examples.event: In person or at an event

row_count.description: Contact rows in the file (blank rows not counted).

check_result.description: The last safety check; null until one finishes, and cleared when the setup changes.

error.description: Why the last check or import failed; empty otherwise.

ImportsMapping.description: Which CSV column (by header name) feeds each field; empty or left out = not in the file. Every named column must exist in the file.

email.description: Required before setup or a check can succeed; the suggested mapping leaves it empty if no header looks like one.

tags.description: Tags separated by commas, semicolons or pipes.

consented_at.description: When they signed up or confirmed.

last_engaged_at.description: Their last click (or activity) in the old tool.

rating.description: Engagement stars 1–5 (e.g. Mailchimp's `MEMBER_RATING`); 4–5 counts as recent activity for people who agreed to tracking.

tracking.description: Per-row click-tracking consent (yes/no); required when `consent.tracking` is `column`.

ImportsConsent.description: Where the contacts came from. Bought, rented, scraped and "I don't know" are deliberately not options. Empty (`{}`) until the import is set up. Nothing is validated when saving; the safety check fails while anything is missing.

source_detail.description: E.g. the platform's name; required for `platform_migration`.

collected_period.description: When they were collected, in words. Required.

wording.description: The consent text they agreed to, or the signup page's URL. Required.

double_opt_in.description: Whether they confirmed by email; makes the contacts' consent basis `double_opt_in`.

tracking.description: Who agreed to click tracking: `all`, `none`, `column` (per row, from `mapping.tracking`), or `eu_by_country` (the default when empty: yes only for a recognised country outside the EU/EEA/UK). People without it are tiered from their opt-in date only and are never Active.

attested.description: The importer signs `attestation_text`. Required for the import to run.

attested_by.description: Set by the server when `attested` is saved; ignored if sent.

topic_ids.description: The brand's topics these people agreed to.

ImportsOutcome.description: What happens to a row. `ready`: imported and can be emailed. `quarantine`: imported, no sign of life for a long time (12 months by default), gets only one re-permission email. `existing`: already a contact; blanks filled in, consent unchanged. `unsubscribed`: an existing contact who unsubscribed; left alone. `suppressed`: blocked company-wide; left out. `role` (info@, sales@…): excluded. `disposable` (throwaway inbox), `invalid`, `no_mailbox` (the domain can't receive mail): rejected. `duplicate`: the same address earlier in the file; skipped.

counts.description: Rows per outcome (only outcomes that occur).

samples.description: Up to 5 addresses per outcome (`line N` for rows without a valid address).

no_tracking.description: Rows to be imported without click-tracking consent.

dates_mapped.description: Whether a signup-date, last-click or rating column is mapped. Without any there is no sign of life to go on, so every new contact is quarantined.

ImportsGate.description: Whether the import may run. Limits are the company's safety limits (2% invalid and 5% role/throwaway by default).

invalid_rate.description: Share of invalid and no-mailbox rows, 0–1.

role_disposable_rate.description: Share of role and throwaway addresses, 0–1.

consent_recorded.description: Whether the consent answers are complete.

problems.description: Why it didn't pass, in words; empty when it did.

updated.description: Existing contacts with blanks filled in.

rejected.description: Invalid, duplicate, role, throwaway and no-mailbox rows.
